facts.statement: The genus Rhacheosaurus was established by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1831 based on skeletal remains from the Late Jurassic of Germany.
facts.quote: The genus was established by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1831 for skeletal remains from the Tithonian (Late Jurassic) of Germany.

facts.statement: A 2009 phylogenetic analysis showed that several long-snouted species previously placed in Geosaurus, Enaliosuchus, and Metriorhynchus were reclassified into Rhacheosaurus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis in 2009 showed that several long-snouted species formerly classified in the related genera Geosaurus, Enaliosuchus, and Metriorhynchus were in fact more closely related to the original specimens of Cricosaurus, and thus were re-classified into this genus.

facts.statement: A 2009 phylogenetic analysis demonstrated that several long-snouted metriorhynchid species formerly classified in Geosaurus, Enaliosuchus, and Metriorhynchus were reclassified into Rhacheosaurus.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético publicado en 2009 demostró que varias especies de metriorrínquidos de hocico alargado antes clasificados en los géneros Geosaurus, Enaliosuchus y Metriorhynchus estaban de hecho más relacionados con los especímenes originales del género Cricosaurus, siendo entonces reclasificados en dicho género.

facts.statement: Rhacheosaurus fossils come from the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic period in Germany.
facts.quote: The genus was established by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1831 for skeletal remains from the Tithonian (Late Jurassic) of Germany.

facts.statement: Rhacheosaurus lived between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago during the Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the lightly built Rhacheosaurus may have specialized in feeding on small prey, while other long-snouted relatives fed mostly on fish.
facts.quote: The long-snouted C. suevicus and R. gracilis would have fed mostly on fish, although the more lightly built Rhacheosaurus may have specialised towards feeding on small prey.

facts.statement: It is debated whether niche partitioning allowed several species of crocodyliforms to coexist in the same environment.
facts.quote: It has been hypothesised that niche partitioning enabled several species of crocodyliforms to co-exist.

rejected.statement: Rhacheosaurus was a small marine crocodyliform belonging to the family Metriorhynchidae.
rejected.quote: Rhacheosaurus is an extinct genus of small marine crocodyliform belonging to the family Metriorhynchidae.
